title: A Torrance plumber's AI voice agent books jobs after 5 p.m.
whatTheyDid: Rob Castelao, owner of Good Guy Plumbing in Torrance, California, told Contractor Magazine that Housecall Pro's CSR AI voice agent answers the phone 24/7, triages the issue, and books the job on the calendar. He said that stopped calls rolling to voicemail after 5 p.m. The same article describes other Housecall Pro AI tools for quotes and follow-up texts. Those are separate from the voice agent.
outcome: Castelao said the impact of the AI tools is still hard to measure directly, and that the company has grown faster this year than in earlier years. The article's figure of more than 500 hours a year is about AI adoption overall, not the voice agent alone.

catches.label: A person still has to override the AI
catches.summary: Castelao said suggestions need a human override, because one AI mistake can lose a customer's trust, and the data the system learns from has to be accurate.

title: Air One replaced an answering service that could not book or speak Spanish
business: Air One Air Conditioning, Heating, Plumbing & Electric
whatTheyDid: Julissa Moulder, CSR and dispatcher at Air One in Colton, California, is quoted in a ServiceTitan story. After 5 p.m. and on weekends, calls went to an answering service that could not book into their software and could not take Spanish calls. They turned on ServiceTitan's AI Virtual Agent, named Jenny, in January. The July 2026 story says that between March and mid-June nearly every lead the company counted converted to a booked call.
outcome: Jenny books in English and Spanish. The story says the old answering service told Spanish-speaking callers it did not know Spanish. The story also says Jenny's booking figure and Moulder's recollection of about 30% conversion on the old summer answering service are not the same period or the same measure.

catches.label: Urgent jobs were offered for the next day until the shop changed the setup
catches.summary: Moulder said Jenny first offered a next-day time for urgent jobs, and customers would not wait. They changed job types so a plumbing emergency could be booked the same night. She said that limit was the setup, not the agent inventing a time.

title: A cleaning company owner says Jobber's receptionist costs him $99 a month
whatTheyDid: Fortune profiled Rick Chorney of Echo Janitorial Services in Abbotsford, British Columbia. He said he spent about half a day connecting an intake form to his job software, turning on an AI receptionist, and sending automatic acknowledgements. Fortune identifies the receptionist as Jobber's. It says the receptionist fields up to 15 calls an hour, including vendor pitches, and escalates only what matters.
cost: Chorney told Fortune he pays $99. The article says a person doing the same phone work would cost roughly $4,000 a month in wages and payroll taxes.
outcome: Fortune says it reviewed his records: about $242,000 two years before the article, just under $1 million the following year, and a $1.3 million projection for the year of the article. The article ties that growth to several AI tools, not to the receptionist alone.

catches.label: The owner said handing over business data felt uncomfortable
catches.summary: Chorney told Fortune that how much information these companies hold is a little scary, and that he still gives the tools his information because it makes the work easier.

title: An LA-area dental office's AI finished 41% of calls that asked for something
whatTheyDid: A page on howdentistsuse.ai, published 20 October 2026, says a part-time staff member read 15 months of call logs from an unnamed dental AI receptionist at an Open Dental general practice near Los Angeles, about $1.5 million in production. Since June 2025 the AI answered overflow and after-hours calls. About half the calls were overflow during busy hours.
cost: The author says the subscription was about $300 a month. He puts the cost at about $400 a month if staff time to return messages is counted, using his own assumption of 10 minutes per callback at $25 an hour. The vendor, contract, and setup fee are not named.
outcome: The page says the office logged 1,432 calls. In 709 the caller was silent or hung up at the greeting. Of 637 calls where someone wanted something done, the AI completed 263 (41%). The page's own arithmetic says bookings, reschedules, and cancellations made on the call totalled 142, including 70 appointments booked. The author later built a competing product. Treat the comparisons on that page with that in mind.

catches.label: Callers could not be transferred to a person
catches.summary: The page says the AI never put a caller through to a person. Across failed calls, the author says only one caller mentioned that it was AI, while callers asked for a person far more often.

Of those, 125 mentioned an AI answering service, a chatbot, or an automated phone system. This is a sample across those trades, not one shop, and the quoted reviews do not name the businesses.
cost: The article's cost table gives a general range of $200 to $2,000 or more a month, or about $1 to $3 per resolution. That is not one vendor's bill, and it is not tied to a named company in the reviews.
outcome: Of the 125 reviews, the article says 78% were negative, 16% neutral, and 6% positive. It says every positive review described an after-hours booking that a person honored.
